title: Obtaining Human Breast Adipose Cells for Breast Cancer Cell Co-culture Studies
protocol: Carefully decant adipose tissue into a sterile Petri dish.
Using a sterile scalpel and forceps, dissociate the tissue mechanically.
Remove any grossly identified undesired tissue types from the adipose sample.
Sterilely drop adipose tissue pieces into a 50 mL tube.
Add PBS to reach a final volume of 50 mL.
Close the tube and shake vigorously by hand for 30 seconds.
Centrifuge the tube for 5 minutes at 400 × g at 22°C–28°C.
Decant the top adipose tissue layer into a new 50 mL tube.
Tilt the tube slowly to an approximately 70 degree angle and use a sterile spoon if necessary.
Repeat steps 4 through 8 until no red pellet can be seen at the bottom of the tube.
Pour the adipose tissue into a new 50 mL tube.
Add the 1 mg/mL Collagenase 1A enzyme solution in a proportion of 1:1 by volume.
Seal the tube with Parafilm.
Place the sealed tube on a vertical tube rotator inside a 37°C CO2 incubator.
Incubate at 37°C for 45 min.
Check for adequate enzymatic digestion after 30 min.
Stop incubation when 80%-90% of the tissue is digested.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 400 × g at 22°C-28°C.
Discard clear yellow layer using a P1000 pipette.
Carefully decant the opaque layer into a new 50 mL tube, avoiding any flow through of media.
Combine tubes if more than one was used for enzymatic digestion.
Place a 200 μm cell strainer into a new 50 mL tube.
Dilute live adipocytes in PBS to bring final volume to 40 ml.
Gently invert the tube to mix and immediately pipette the suspended adipocytes onto the 200 μm cell strainer.
Add 3 mL of fresh PBS on top if the cell strainer becomes blocked, and resuspend by gently pipetting.
Replace the filter to complete sample filtration if necessary.
Centrifuge filtered adipocytes for 5 min at 400 × g at 22°C–28°C.
Aspirate media from tubes containing the SVF.
Add 40 mL of PBS and resuspend the pellet.
Combine pellets from multiple tubes into one tube if used for enzymatic digestion.
Bring total volume to 40 mL in PBS after combining pellets.
Place a 70 μm cell strainer into a new 50 mL tube.
Filter the cell suspension through the cell strainer.
Centrifuge the filtered SVF for 5 min at 400 × g at 22°C–28°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully to avoid losing the SVF pellet.
Resuspend the SVF pellet in DMEM media supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Seed cells at a concentration of 300,000 cells/cm² for culture.
Count only the big cells (hASC) to estimate numbers for plating.
Maintain cultures for 2–3 passages, replacing media every 2 days.
Culture hASC until cells reach 100% confluence.

Induce adipogenesis by three cycles of induction/maintenance as follows: culture for 3 days with supplemented adipogenesis induction medium, followed by 1-3 days in supplemented adipogenic maintenance media.
After three complete cycles of induction/maintenance, continue culturing the differentiating adipocytes for 7 more days in adipogenic maintenance medium.

Seed a non-confluent asynchronous culture of the chosen breast cancer cell line onto a 6-well plate using appropriate culture media the day before recovering mature adipocytes from a fresh human breast fat sample.

Resuspend the mature human mammary adipocytes obtained after isolation in the culture medium suitable for the specific breast cancer cell line, using 5 mL of media/mL final volume of isolated adipocytes.
Remove and discard the culture media from breast cancer cell cultures.
Gently invert the tube containing mature adipocytes to mix.
Pipette 2 mL of resuspended adipocytes into each well.
Add 500 μL of fresh culture media to each well every 2 days.
Do not complete change of media during co-culture assays.
At day 7, breast cancer cells and mature adipocytes can be easily separated due to different attachment to the cell culture surface.
Collect mature adipocytes by recovering the media using a P1000 pipette.
Centrifuge the tube containing the media and adipocytes for 5 min at 400 × g at 22°C–28°C.
Aspirate the media to collect mature adipocytes.
Remove the culture media from immature adherent cultures of adipocytes.
Seed breast cancer cells on top of immature adipocytes.
Add culture medium appropriate to the breast cancer line.
For MCF7 cells, seed 400,000 cells/P100 dish and use 7 mL of IMEM + 5% FBS + 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
For MDA-MB-231 cells, seed same cell amount but use 7 mL of DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
It is highly recommended to use fluorescent-tagged breast cancer cells for isolation after co-culture.
Change culture media every 2 days.
Discard culture media from hASC cultures obtained.
Seed breast cancer cells on top of hASC using the appropriate culture media for the breast cancer line.
Use fluorescent-tagged breast cancer cells to facilitate their isolation from hASC after co-culture.
Change culture media every 2 days during co-culture.
At day 7, trypsinize the breast cancer cells and hASC.
Recover and wash the cells after trypsinization.
Separate breast cancer cells and hASC using FACS.
Use anti-cytokeratin as a marker for epithelial cells or fluorescence if the cancer line is GFP-tagged for sorting.
